ground_truth.what_company_does: A premium non-alcoholic functional beverage designed for social settings as a healthier alternative to alcohol and mixers.
ground_truth.business_model: Consumer packaged goods (CPG) company selling beverages through on-premise venues and retail distribution
ground_truth.revenue_model: Per-unit beverage sales to venues and distributors, with revenue driven by product velocity and repeat purchases
ground_truth.go_to_market: Direct sales to nightlife venues and hospitality operators followed by expansion through distributors and retail channels
ground_truth.target_customer: Hospitality venues such as nightclubs, restaurants, and hotels, with end consumers being health-conscious social drinkers
ground_truth.traction_summary: Early traction with approximately $100K run-rate, initial venue adoption, and product usage in high-end venues, but most forward revenue is based on LOIs and pipeline rather than realized sales
ground_truth.market_positioning: Premium healthy social beverage positioned as a replacement or complement to alcohol in social environments
ground_truth.competitive_differentiation: Combination of functional ingredients, premium branding, and positioning as a status-enhancing non-alcoholic beverage
key_strengths: Clear wedge into nightlife and premium on-premise venues
Early signs of product-market fit through venue usage
Strong founder network in hospitality and nightlife
Premium branding and positioning aligned with target demographic
key_risks: Low actual revenue relative to projected pipeline
Reliance on LOIs and projected sales rather than confirmed revenue
Highly competitive beverage market with low barriers to entry
Unproven repeat purchase behavior at scale
investor_relevance_notes: This is an early-stage CPG company with initial traction but limited revenue scale
Key question is whether venue-level demand translates into repeatable consumer demand
Pipeline and LOIs should not be treated as realized revenue
Success depends heavily on distribution and brand strength
Unit economics and margins are not clearly defined in the deck
